body:
sara: FYI support received multiple customer reports ~11:10am UTC of API returning 500s on inference calls, customer says started after morning deploy. They expect 429 for throttles.
sara: stacktraces from the customer attached (they're hitting the /v1/generate route).
sara: can someone triage? Ticket: #CS-2489.

zoe: I'm on it. Looking at our gateway logs now, I see a spike of 503/500s from the rate-limiter upstream between 11:06-11:12.
zoe: quick grep: `grep "rate-limiter" gateway.log | sed -n '11000,11050p'` shows many `502`/`503` and some `500` with "upstream timeout".

mike: I see a recent routing tweak in the canary config that preferentially routes low-priority customers to the new rlimit pool. Deploy was at 11:02 (deploy-bot confirms). Could be misroute.

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary/routing-config v2.17 deployed by anna at 2024-10-22T11:02:14Z.

anna: I pushed a small change to the rate-limiter traffic-split to test the new pool. Didn't expect connection exhaustion. Rolling back now.

zoe: Repro steps from infra:
1) curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
2) observe either 500 or 429 depending on path.

mike: Captured logs from rate-limiter instance (truncated):
```
2024-10-22T11:07:08Z ERROR quota-orch] request_id=abc123 status=500 error="connection pool exhausted" backend=quota-db
2024-10-22T11:07:08Z WARN  quota-orch] falling back to default handler -> returned 500
2024-10-22T11:07:09Z INFO  gateway] proxied->quota-orch timeout
```

zoe: That `falling back to default handler` path maps to an internal 500 response rather than converting to 429. There's a routing fallback that assumes a quota service 4xx/429. If the quota orchestrator times out it hits the fallback which currently returns 500.

sara: Customers are upset because docs say we'll return 429 on rate limit. They're getting 500, which triggers retries and makes it worse. Escalation opened with account team.

mike: Immediate mitigation: rolling back the canary to stop sending traffic to the new rlimit pool (announced in #eng-runtime). Performing now.

deploy-bot: rollback event: canary/routing-config rolled back to v2.16 by mike at 2024-10-22T11:12:03Z.

ops-oncall: After rollback traffic normalised, error rate went down ~95% by 11:18. Monitoring still watching.

zoe: Root cause hypothesis: new rlimit pool has an exporter/connection leak under certain high-concurrency patterns -> quota-orchestrator exhausted DB/connections and timed out. Fallback path not mapping timeouts to 429. So two issues: (A) rlimit pool leak/connection exhaustion, (B) fallback handler returns 500 not 429 for dependency timeout.

anna: Repro locally by running a short script that fires 200 concurrent requests with small token budgets. I can reproduce the connection exhaustion within ~30s. Will attach repro script.

anna: Repro script (trimmed):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -sS -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
wait
```
Observed 30% 500s and many timeouts from quota service.

mike: Short-term fixes: 
- Revert routing (done).
- Add a circuit-breaker on gateway -> quota-orch path to convert dependency timeouts to 429 when capacity signals are present (config change).
- Increase connection pool limits on quota-orch instances until we have a patch.

zoe: I'll open two PRs: one to adjust the fallback mapping (timeout -> 429) and one to add better telemetry (per-circuit drop counts).

sara: Communicating to customers: message drafted to affected accounts explaining we rolled back and are investigating. Will offer rate-limit headers explanation and postmortem follow-up.

mike: Longer term: root fix in quota-orch to patch the leak, add unit tests (stress tests) for high concurrent small-token workloads, and a canary guard to block the new rlimit pool if error rates spike >1% in first 2 mins.

zoe: Action items (short list):
- anna: upload repro script + stack traces to the incident folder (due EOD).
- mike: temp pool size bump + revert config (done).
- zoe: PRs for fallback mapping and telemetry (ETA 4h).
- sara: customer comms + open CS followups.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2024-11022 by zoe. Severity: P2.

sara: Thanks team. I'll keep the account managers posted. Will update this thread with the postmortem link once complete. :thumbsup:

zoe: monitoring note: watching error rate and latency, will escalate to P1 if >5% errors for 10m.

mike: adding a log snippet of the gateway proxy rule that did mapping (for the record):
```
# gateway routing snippet
route "quota-orch" {
  try_pools = ["rlimit-v2","rlimit-v1"]
  on_timeout = "fallback_default_handler" # currently returns 500 -> change to map_timeout_to_429
}
```

anna: I'll PR the fix for `fallback_default_handler` to map timeouts to 429 and add a test verifying retry semantics.

sara: last note: reopened CS ticket to mark as "mitigated" for customers while we work on permanent fixes.

ops-oncall: marking incident as monitoring. Update if anything changes.
